newsitem.title: USA: Unitog Q4 hurt by direct sales falloff.
newsitem.headline: Unitog Q4 hurt by direct sales falloff.

text.p: Unitog Co, which rents and sells uniforms to a variety of industries, said it posted lower January 26 fourth-quarter earnings because of a decrease in its direct sales business.

Chairman Randolph Rolf in a statement also cited additional costs associated with the introduction of a new data processing system at Unitog's distribution centers and slower than expected progress in improving the Michigan-based rental operations acquired in March, 1996 from Central Quality Services Corp.
Fourth-quarter total revenues rose to $66.5 million from $60.5 million.

"Rental revenues increased 16 percent to $53 million during the quarter due to our recent acquisitions and revenue growth at existing locations," Rolf noted. "Direct sales declined by seven percent from the previous year to $14 million. The decrease was primarily the result of customer shipment delays created by the introduction of a new data processing system in our distribution centers."
Earnings in the quarter fell to $0.29 a share from $0.32.
